headline: High: shared web-facing, file-capable defaults create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action risk between open-webui and RD-Agent.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: open-webui ingests browser, MCP, OpenAPI, and file content by default, while RD-Agent can browse and send outputs through LLM/API workflows. The pair has a plausible instruction-hijack path if open-webui forwards untrusted content into RD-Agent or vice versa, but no shared channel is explicitly documented, so uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF open-webui forwards untrusted web/file/MCP content into RD-Agent prompts without sanitization
IF either agent treats the other's output as instructions rather than data
mitigations: Disable MCP/OpenAPI tool servers for the pair during testing
Add a fixed delimiter and instruction-stripping preprocessor
Require manual review of any cross-agent prompt payload
Use separate workspaces for each agent
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all forwarded content

B_data_leakage.rationale: open-webui explicitly touches files, persistent memory, and API keys, while RD-Agent touches logs and financial/research data and uses broad network egress. If they share a workspace or credentials, sensitive prompts, files, or keys can flow from open-webui into RD-Agent outputs or external APIs. The blast radius includes secrets and research data, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF the two agents share a filesystem, mounted volume, or credential store
IF open-webui forwards files or memory into RD-Agent-backed API calls
mitigations: Separate mounts and secret stores immediately
Rotate any shared API keys before pairing
Disable file upload forwarding between agents
Review logs for accidental secret propagation
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention policies

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have broad network egress and browser access, and open-webui can spawn subprocesses while RD-Agent runs multi-instance research workflows. That creates overlapping write/side-effect potential on shared resources, but the profiles do not prove a shared mutable directory or lockless git/database target, so medium is the safest supported level.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same filesystem, git repo, or database
IF orchestration does not provide locking or per-agent namespaces
mitigations: Assign distinct output directories
Run each agent in its own container namespace
Serialize writes to shared resources
Check for concurrent git operations before enabling both
requires-engineering: add resource locks around mutable stores

D_cascading_error.rationale: open-webui can surface model outputs, files, and tool results, and RD-Agent is a research automation system that can act on LLM-generated outputs. If RD-Agent consumes open-webui content without verification, errors or hallucinations can cascade into downstream research artifacts or actions. The profiles suggest the pathway but do not document a direct autonomous action chain, so medium fits.
conditions: IF RD-Agent treats open-webui output as authoritative input without validation
IF open-webui forwards unverified citations, code, or plans into RD-Agent workflows
mitigations: Require source verification before RD-Agent acts
Insert a human approval step for cross-agent outputs
Limit open-webui to read-only summarization for RD-Agent inputs
Compare outputs against original sources before execution
requires-engineering: add confidence and provenance checks

E_compliance.rationale: open-webui handles chat messages, documents, notes, calendar events, files, and API keys, while RD-Agent handles financial reports, competition datasets, and logs. If the pair is used on regulated or residency-bound data, their differing storage and API paths can create retention or jurisdiction mismatches. The profiles do not specify a concrete residency regime, so medium is appropriate rather than high.
conditions: IF regulated data such as EU PII, PHI, or financial records is routed through both agents
IF retention or deletion policies differ between open-webui storage and RD-Agent logs
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair by policy
Document retention settings for both systems
Purge logs after each run
Use region-matched API endpoints
requires-engineering: implement data-class-specific retention controls
